failure.target: P(max_{1 <= j <= m_n} |X_{n,j}| > eps) -> 0 as n -> infinity.
failure.evidence: Take X_{n,j} independent Bernoulli(1/n) and m_n = n^2: each fixed j has P(|X_{n,j}| > eps) = 1/n -> 0 when 0 < eps < 1, and zero when eps >= 1; also m_n -> infinity. Thus both hypotheses hold, whereas P(max_{1<=j<=m_n} |X_{n,j}| > 1/2) = 1 - (1 - 1/n)^{n^2} -> 1.

computation.output_excerpt: n=10,100,1000 with m_n=n^2: P(max > 1/2) = 0.999973, 1.000000, 1.000000 -> 1, never -> 0 (exact rational arithmetic)
